subject: Automotive & EVs
title: The Charging Curve
description: Learn The Charging Curve in one minute.

hook.text: Fast charging an EV is not like filling a gas tank—the speed drops dramatically as the battery fills up.

buildup.text: From 10 to 50 percent, fast chargers pump energy in at maximum speed with almost no resistance.

discovery.text: Above 80 percent, charging slows to a crawl because pushing more ions in risks overheating the cells.

twist.text: That's why the advice is to charge to 80 percent on road trips—the last 20 takes as long as the first 60.

climax.text: Understanding the charging curve saves enormous time on long trips compared to charging to 100 each stop.

punchline.text: The fastest strategy is to stop charging before the battery is full.

quiz.question: Why does EV fast charging slow down above 80 percent?
options: The charger runs out of power
Pushing more ions risks overheating the cells
The car's computer limits it for no reason

details.summary: An EV's charging speed follows a curve that starts fast when the battery is low and tapers off as it fills, similar to pouring water into a glass that resists being topped off to avoid overflow.
details.whyItMatters: Understanding the charging curve explains why charging from 10 to 80 percent is fast but the last 20 percent takes much longer, which shapes efficient long-distance EV travel strategies.
takeaways: Peak charging speed occurs between roughly 10 and 50 percent
Speed tapers above 80 percent to protect battery health
Road trip charging is fastest when stopping at 10 to 20 percent

faq.question: Why does charging slow down above 80 percent?
faq.answer: As cells approach full capacity, the voltage rises and ions have fewer open spots to settle into the anode. The BMS reduces current to prevent overcharging, overheating, and accelerated cell degradation.

faq.question: Should EV owners routinely charge to 100 percent?
faq.answer: For daily use, charging to 80 or 90 percent is recommended to reduce stress on the battery. Charging to 100 percent is fine before a long trip but should not be the everyday routine.
